quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When passing a truck on a two-lane road, when should you return to your lane?

options.text: When you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
As soon as the truck is behind you.
When you feel you have enough space.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Wait until you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes so they work together when you use the rear brake.
It brakes automatically based on how you usually ride.
It applies the brake when you shift down to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes so they work together when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems that connect the front and rear brakes. When you apply the rear brake, both brakes work together. Check your owner's manual to learn about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do both actions at the same time.
Only brake.
Do one action, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you need to brake and swerve, do them separately. Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake. Never do both at the same time.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, where is the safest place to ride?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
Pull onto the shoulder and wait for the rain to stop.
In the tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Roads are slippery when rain first starts, especially in the center of the lane. Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles. The left tire track is usually safest.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles traveling at 25 mph or slower, such as construction equipment, farm machinery, or horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: When entering a curve, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
Where you can see best and be seen best.
In the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can see best and be seen best.
questions.explanation: Position your motorcycle in a curve to improve your view and make sure others can see you. In a left curve, ride on the right side of your lane to spot oncoming traffic early. In a right curve, ride on the left side to see ahead without getting too close to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: _______ of motorcycle and car collisions happen because drivers fail to yield to the motorcyclist.

options.text: One-quarter
More than half
One-half

questions.correctAnswerText: More than half
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car collisions happen because drivers do not yield the right-of-way to motorcyclists. Never assume drivers will yield, even if they are supposed to.

questions.question: A helmet gives the most protection if it has all of these qualities, except:

options.text: Meets U.S. DOT standards.
Loose-fitting.
No cracks or damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loose-fitting.
questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet U.S. DOT standards, fit snugly, and have no damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. A loose helmet does not protect you well.

questions.question: If you carry a passenger on your motorcycle, what should you do with your tire pressure?

options.text: Lower it.
Leave it the same.
Increase it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase it.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You will likely need to add a few pounds of pressure to your tires. Check your owner's manual for the right pressure.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions separately. Never brake while swerving because your motorcycle could fall over.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on a straight road:

options.text: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You must release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can keep it locked until you stop. A locked rear wheel usually does not cause you to lose control if the motorcycle stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in residential areas when no sign is posted?

options.text: 20 mph
25 mph
30 mph
40 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 30 mph
questions.explanation: The speed limit in residential and business areas is 30 mph. Always follow posted signs if a different limit is shown.

questions.question: What does eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: They see you.
It does not mean they will yield to you properly.
They will definitely yield to you properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will yield to you properly.
questions.explanation: Do not assume eye contact means another driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but still fail to see them.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can be operated:

options.text: Only during the day.
Without a driver license.
With any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: With any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any class of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: What is a main cause of single-vehicle motorcycle crashes?

options.text: Riding too fast for weather conditions.
Turning too wide in a curve.
Running off the road to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning too wide in a curve.
questions.explanation: A main cause of single-vehicle crashes is turning too wide in a curve. This can cause a motorcycle to leave the road or hit an object.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: There is usually an oily strip in the center of a traffic lane. Motorcyclists should:

options.text: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
Not worry about the oil and grease.
Find the lane with the least oil and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
questions.explanation: Avoid riding on oil and grease buildup. The oily strip is usually only about two feet wide, so you can often stay to the left or right of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: How are convex mirrors different from regular mirrors?

options.text: They show a narrower view of the road.
They show a wider view of the road.
They show a better view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors on motorcycles show a wider view of the road than flat mirrors. However, they can make vehicles behind you look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: What color are service signs?

options.text: Orange with black letters.
Blue with white letters.
Green with white letters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters. They show where you can find rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: The oily strip in the center of a lane:

options.text: Should always be avoided.
Usually provides good traction unless it is raining.
Should only be used when sharing the lane with another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually provides good traction unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily strip usually provides enough traction for safe riding, except when it is raining. Since the strip is usually only about two feet wide, you can ride on either side of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: Oil drippings and debris often collect in ______ of a lane.

options.text: The left side
The middle
The right side

questions.correctAnswerText: The middle
questions.explanation: Oil drippings and debris from cars and trucks collect in the center of a lane.

questions.question: When being passed, moving to the part of your lane farthest from the passing vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be farther from the passing vehicle.
Is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
Does not affect safety either way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: When being passed, do not move to the farthest part of your lane. This may signal the passing driver to return to your lane too early.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Show a narrow view of the road behind you.
Show a wide view of the road behind you.
Are illegal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you than flat mirrors. They also make objects look farther away than they really are. Take time to adjust to convex mirrors if your motorcycle has them.

questions.question: To make a quick turn, you should:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Make your motorcycle lean quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make your motorcycle lean quickly.
questions.explanation: To make a quick turn, make your motorcycle lean fast in the direction you want to turn. The sharper the turn, the more your motorcycle must lean.

questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, you should always:

options.text: Lean in the direction of the curve.
Slow down while in the turn.
Turn using only the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean in the direction of the curve.
questions.explanation: When turning, always lean in the direction of the turn. Slow down before you enter the turn.
